text: In the nineties, a whole encyclopedia fit on one disc, and it worked with no internet. Today, many children share one phone and a patchy connection.
Awari brings the disc back: a free encyclopedia that keeps working when the internet does not.
You explore it by place, by date, or by playing. Four hundred and eighty-three articles, every country, and more than three thousand pictures, all openly licensed.
Spin the globe, and pick a country.
Each article has pictures, quick facts, and a quiz. Tap any word to look it up.
Every question has three hints. A wrong answer is a chance to look again. A right answer inks a stamp, and shows the sentence that proves it.
In the Castle, each answer lights the next door.
The timeline walks through fifteen hundred dated events.
And the picture library shows who made each picture, and its licence.
Now the connection drops. Articles, quizzes, the atlas and the castle all keep working, just like the disc did.
I built Awari with Kiro Crew. Every session began from steering files and specs.
Steering loaded the design rules before any code was written.
Agent hooks ran lint, tests and licence checks after every change.
Custom crew members, a design reviewer and a licence auditor, checked the work independently.
Twenty-eight specs and more than six hundred tests guard the rules that matter.
